elements.text:
E1 Joint mobility and general leg strengthening
Knee OA, Degenerative meniscus, Baker’s cyst w/ joint disease, Hip OA, Pesanserine pain

Gentle bending and strengthening: heel slides or seated knee bends
Sit-to-stand: rise slowly from chair, can use hands if needed
Standing hip abduction: Move leg sideways while holding supports
Low step-ups and short walking bouts: gradually build strength and endurance

E2 Knee and Hip Strength with Movement Control
Patellofemoral pain & ITB syndrome; Patellar dislocation or recurrent instability after clearance from doctor

Shallow squats or chair rises
Bridges: Lift pelvis with both feet planted
Low step-downs: lower slowly from a small step, keeping the pelvis steady, progress to supported single-leg balance.

E3 Hip Joint Strength Within Comfortable Movement
Nonarthritic hip-related pain: suspected FAI, labral pathology, or dysplasia 

Bridges
Standing hip abduction and extension
High chair sit-to-stand
Supported balance: Practice steps and getting in and out of vehicles (or some alternative) within a comfortable range

E4 Progressive Quadriceps and Patellar Tendon Loading
Patellar tendinopathy

Static knee-extension holds or a shallow wall-sit: only if tolerated
Slow chair-rises, squats, and step-ups once ↑ is comfortable 
Add resistance once ↑ is comfortable
Introduce hopping afterwards

E5 Lateral Hip Strengthening with Reduced Tendon Compression
Gluteal tendinopathy 

Seated outward press: gently press the knees outward against a band without moving
Progress to standing hip abduction, bridges, low step-ups, and supported single-leg control

E6 Progressive Hamstring Strengthening
Hamstring strain & Proximal hamstring tendinopathy

Heel dig holds: lying with knees bent, press the heels into the floor
Progress to bridges, resisted knee bends, and shallow hip hinges
Gradually increase resistance and introduce controlled lengthening exercises

E7 Groin, Hip, and Trunk Strengthening
Adductor-related; iliopsoas-related; inguinal-related; pubic-related groin pain

Shared base: bridges and gentle abdominal bracing
Adductor/pubic branch: pillow squeezes between the knees, then resisted inward leg movement
Iliopsoas branch: seated knee-lift holds against the hand, then resisted marching
Inguinal branch: graded trunk exercises without painful straining

E8 Protected Knee Injury Rehabilitation
ACL injury, traumatic meniscus injury, MCL/LCL sprain, PCL injury

Quadriceps tightening and permitted knee movement
Followed by chair rises, shallow squats, step-ups, and balance training as restrictions allow
Eventually practice work-related tasks
